title: 19 Nov 2026
note: Notes for 19 November 2026 from The Hindu’s Delhi edition of 19 November (the pages supplied) and from news reports and official releases. Where only the headline was available (the three Supreme Court items of that day), the note gives the background to the story, and the facts behind each news item come from standard textbooks and official sources. The paper’s editorials and opinion pieces are presented as the writers’ views.

topics.t: Supreme Court: Gram Sabha consent is mandatory for mining land acquisition in tribal areas
topics.news: According to the Supreme Court’s daily round-up for 19 November, the Court quashed a mining land acquisition in a tribal area and held that Gram Sabha consent is mandatory. Only the headline of the ruling was available, so the note gives the legal background.

rows: Fifth Schedule
Article 244(1): Scheduled Areas are administered with a Governor’s special powers to regulate transfer of tribal land.
PESA, 1996
The Gram Sabha must be consulted before land is acquired in Scheduled Areas and before minor minerals are leased.
Land Acquisition Act, 2013
Section 41 requires the prior consent of the Gram Sabha for acquisition in Scheduled Areas.
Samatha (1997)
The Court barred leases of tribal land to private mining companies in Scheduled Areas.
Niyamgiri (2013)
In the Orissa Mining Corporation case the Court asked Gram Sabhas to decide on the religious and cultural rights of the Dongria Kondh under the Forest Rights Act.

ul: **Why consent matters:** mining in Scheduled Areas displaces communities that depend on forest and land, so consent is the main safeguard.
**Mines and Minerals Act, 1957:** the Act governs mining leases; the tribal-land safeguards sit alongside it.

prel.d: The body of all adult voters of a village; central to decisions under PESA.
Governs the administration of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes in most States.
Barred private mining leases in Scheduled Areas.
Prior Gram Sabha consent for acquisition in Scheduled Areas.

qs.q: Examine the constitutional and legal safeguards for tribal land against mining and development projects.
Discuss the role of the Gram Sabha under PESA and the Forest Rights Act.

topics.t: Supreme Court dismisses the ED’s challenge to Azam Khan’s interim bail
topics.news: Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan walked out of Ghaziabad jail on Wednesday, a day after the Allahabad High Court granted him interim bail in a money-laundering case investigated by the Enforcement Directorate and linked to his Mohammad Ali Jauhar Trust, which runs a university in Uttar Pradesh. He said his only crime was that a Muslim had built an educational institution, and party chief Akhilesh Yadav welcomed the release. The Hindu reports that the Supreme Court has declined the ED’s plea against the interim bail, as the Court’s 19 November round-up also lists. The note adds the background on bail in money-laundering cases and links to the 18 November note on mala fide.

rows: PMLA section 45
Bail needs the Court to be satisfied that there are reasonable grounds to believe the accused is not guilty and is not likely to commit an offence on bail (the **twin conditions**).
Case law
Nikesh Tarachand Shah (2017) struck down the twin conditions; they were restored by a 2018 amendment and upheld in Vijay Madanlal Choudhary (2022).
Bail is the rule
In Manish Sisodia v. ED (2024) the Court said bail is the rule and jail the exception, even under the PMLA.
Interim bail
Temporary relief for a limited period or purpose, given while the main bail plea or trial is pending.

ul: **Challenge by the agency:** an appeal against bail asks whether the order was perverse or ignored relevant facts; cancelling bail needs strong reasons.
**Personal liberty:** Article 21 weighs against long pre-trial custody.

prel.d: The two tests for bail in Section 45 of the PMLA.
Short-term bail granted pending a final decision on bail.
Judgment upholding key provisions of the PMLA, including Section 45.
The agency that investigates money laundering under the PMLA.

qs.q: Discuss how courts balance personal liberty and the need for custodial investigation in bail decisions under special laws such as the PMLA.
What is mala fide in administrative and criminal law? Explain how courts test an allegation of mala fide.

topics.t: Delhi voter-roll revision: complaint of fraudulent Form 7 applications
topics.news: The Supreme Court on 19 November directed the Election Commission and Delhi’s Chief Electoral Officer to examine a complaint by Congress leader Ali Mehdi that fraudulent Form 7 applications were filed to delete voters in the Mustafabad constituency during the Special Intensive Revision, and said remedial steps must follow if the allegations prove true. This is based on the Court’s daily round-up headline.

blocks.h: How the electoral roll is kept

rows: Constitution
Article 324 gives the Election Commission superintendence, direction and control of the preparation of electoral rolls; Article 326 provides adult suffrage.
Law
The Representation of the People Act, 1950 (sections 21 to 23) deals with preparing and revising rolls and including names.
Forms
Form 6 is for new voters, **Form 7** is an objection to a name or a request to delete it, and Form 8 is for corrections.
Special Intensive Revision
A door-to-door re-verification of the entire roll, used in several States; the notes of 13 and 14 November cover the exercise.

ul: **Deletion safeguards:** a name should be removed only after notice and a hearing to the voter.
**Misuse of Form 7:** bulk or false objections can wrongly remove voters, which is why complaints are examined at the level of the Electoral Registration Officer.

prel.d: Vests superintendence and control of elections in the Election Commission.
Used to object to the inclusion of a name or to seek deletion from the electoral roll.
A full re-verification of the voter list.
Governs electoral rolls and the qualification and registration of voters.

qs.q: Discuss the role of the Election Commission in maintaining the integrity of electoral rolls. What safeguards protect a voter from wrongful deletion?
Examine the issues raised by the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls.

topics.t: Turning police reform into practice: the Indian Police Foundation’s change manual
topics.news: R. K. Vij, a former IPS officer, writes that people still hesitate to visit a police station, while police personnel complain of heavy workloads and too few weekly rest days. The Indian Police Foundation (set up on 21 October 2015), with the Azim Premji Foundation, has run a project on ‘internal police reforms’ with interviews at 15 police stations in Punjab, Telangana and Tamil Nadu, and has prepared a ‘change manual’ to be first applied in Punjab and then in the other two States. Its four focus areas: better complaint and FIR registration and police response (e-FIR under the BNSS, a visitor management system, QR codes); crime prevention and community outreach (a night safety escort scheme for working women, CCTV, a citizen sentinel scheme); prevention of misconduct and harassment (scrutiny of the reasons for arrest at DySP level, a phone call to a relative after arrest, free legal aid, videography of personal searches, online monitoring of lock-ups); and better working conditions (rest rooms, weekly offs, vehicle allowances, a contingency fund, a tablet for each investigating officer to use the e-Sakshya app, a recruitment board). Most proposals need no extra budget.

rows: Constitution
‘Police’ and ‘public order’ are State subjects (Entries 2 and 1 of the State List), so reform depends on the States.
Prakash Singh case (2006)
The Supreme Court directed seven reforms, among them fixed tenure for police chiefs, a State Security Commission, separation of investigation from law and order, and a Police Complaints Authority.
New criminal laws
The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 allows e-complaints (signed within three days) and zero FIRs, and the e-Sakshya app records searches and seizures.
Working conditions
Long hours and no weekly off reduce the quality of investigation and the behaviour of police towards the public.
Model Police Act
A 2006 draft law prepared by an expert committee for States to adopt.

ul: **Station-level reform:** most of the proposals can be applied at the police station and cost little.
**Phased rollout:** testing in one State before wider use lets the reforms be adjusted to local conditions.

prel.d: Think tank for police reform, set up on 21 October 2015.
Supreme Court directions for seven police reforms.
BNSS provisions for online complaints and registration of an FIR at any police station.
App for recording evidence collected during searches and seizures.

qs.q: Discuss the need for police reforms in India. Why has the implementation of the Supreme Court’s directions been slow?
How do the new criminal laws change the way police register complaints and conduct arrests and searches?

topics.t: Sacrilege at a Tilak Nagar gurdwara: arrest and calls for a probe
topics.news: The Delhi police on Wednesday arrested a 40-year-old man for allegedly desecrating the Guru Granth Sahib at a gurdwara in west Delhi’s Tilak Nagar on Sunday. Police are also looking into claims that some gurdwara management committee members tried to hide the incident for two days. After a complaint by the gurdwara management on Tuesday, an FIR was registered under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita Sections 192 (provocation with intent to cause riot), 298 (defiling a place of worship) and 299 (acts intended to outrage religious feelings). A separate complaint was filed against five members of the panel. Delhi Sikh Gurdwara Management Committee president Harmeet Singh Kalka called the incident deeply distressing, sought strict action and asked the Lieutenant-Governor to take cognisance and urged gurdwara committees to install CCTV cameras and strengthen security.

rows: BNS offences

Sections 298 and 299 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 deal with damaging or defiling a place of worship and with deliberate acts to outrage religious feelings; they replace Sections 295 and 295A of the Indian Penal Code.
Religious freedom
Articles 25 and 26 protect freedom of religion and the right of religious denominations to manage their affairs, subject to public order, morality and health.
Gurdwara management
In Delhi, gurdwaras are managed by the Delhi Sikh Gurdwara Management Committee under the Delhi Sikh Gurdwara Act, 1971; the Sikh Gurdwaras Act, 1925 governs the SGPC in Punjab.
Law and order
Public order is a State subject, but in Delhi the Union Government controls the police.

ul: **Public order:** quick arrest and investigation are meant to calm tension and prevent reprisals.
**Accountability of managers:** the question is whether those in charge hid the incident, which is being examined.

prel.d: Damaging or defiling a place of worship or object held sacred.
Deliberate and malicious acts intended to outrage religious feelings.
Delhi Sikh Gurdwara Management Committee, set up under the 1971 Act.
Freedom of religion and of religious affairs.

qs.q: Discuss how the Constitution and criminal law balance freedom of religion and the protection of religious sentiments.
Why is the control of police in Delhi different from that in other States?

topics.t: ICJ finds Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya
topics.news: On 19 November 2026 the International Court of Justice ruled in The Gambia v. Myanmar that Myanmar’s 2017 ‘clearance operations’ in northern Rakhine State violated its obligations under the Genocide Convention. The Court found that Myanmar had not directly and publicly incited genocide by private persons, and that it breached the Court’s 2020 order on provisional measures by failing to prevent the destruction of evidence and genocidal acts. Reparations were left to a later phase, with Myanmar to report within two years on restitution measures and proposed compensation. The judgment is final and binding, with no appeal.

rows: Genocide Convention, 1948

Defines genocide as acts such as killing or causing serious harm committed with intent to destroy a national, ethnic, racial or religious group in whole or in part. Article IX gives the ICJ jurisdiction over disputes between parties.
The case
The Gambia filed it in November 2019; the Court ordered provisional measures in January 2020 and rejected Myanmar’s preliminary objections in July 2022.
Rohingya
A Muslim minority of Rakhine State, denied citizenship in Myanmar under the 1982 law. More than seven lakh fled to Bangladesh after the August 2017 military operations.
ICJ
The UN’s principal judicial organ, at The Hague, with 15 judges elected for nine-year terms by the General Assembly and Security Council. It decides disputes **between States**.
ICC
The International Criminal Court tries **individuals** under the Rome Statute; India is not a party.

ul: **Enforcement:** the ICJ has no police power; under Article 94 of the UN Charter a party can go to the Security Council, where a veto can block action.
**India’s link:** India is a party to the Genocide Convention (it enacted the Genocide Convention Act, 1960), hosts Rohingya refugees, and is not a party to the 1951 Refugee Convention.
**Non-refoulement:** the principle that a person should not be sent back to a place where they face serious harm.

prel.d: UN treaty that defines and prohibits genocide.
ICJ case filed in 2019; the merits judgment of 19 November 2026 found Myanmar in breach.
The ICJ settles disputes between States; the ICC prosecutes individuals.
No return of a person to a place where they face persecution or serious harm.

qs.q: Discuss the role of the International Court of Justice in upholding international law. What are the limits on enforcing its judgments?
Examine the Rohingya crisis and its implications for India’s refugee and neighbourhood policy.

topics.t: Many imperatives: India’s partnerships after the Manila summits
topics.news: The Hindu’s editorial says the summits in Manila had many imperatives: they were the first ASEAN summits since the U.S.–Israel attacks on Iran and Iran’s blockade of Hormuz and strikes on Gulf countries upended energy and trade across South and South East Asia. Prime Minister Modi’s call for ‘peace, stability and predictability’ at the East Asia Summit was aimed as much at leaders of the U.S., Russia and China as at the region. India and the Philippines have deepened ties since President Marcos’s visit to Delhi in August 2025, including an upgraded Strategic Partnership, maritime exchanges and talks on supplying more Indian-made BrahMos missile batteries. For the first time a Quad leaders’ summit was held in a non-Quad country, hosted by the U.S. on the sidelines. Outcomes: a new ASEAN–India cooperation on disaster management; a focus on cyber-crime at the East Asia Summit; free tourist visas for all ASEAN citizens; a Quad Business Leaders Forum in Mumbai next year; and the first Quad naval exercises with patrol aircraft. The editorial says these paled beside the anticipated three-way summit of Mr Trump, Mr Putin and Mr Xi in Shenzhen, which New Delhi must watch closely.

rows: ASEAN summits
The ASEAN–India Summit and the East Asia Summit are held every year when ASEAN meets; ASEAN has 11 members and the Philippines is chair in 2026.
India–Philippines
BrahMos, the supersonic cruise missile built by an Indo-Russian joint venture, was exported first to the Philippines under a 2022 contract; the ties rest on a shared interest in the South China Sea.
Quad
India, the U.S., Japan and Australia; a leaders’ summit outside a member country shows the grouping’s link with ASEAN.
Free visas
Free or relaxed visas raise tourism and people-to-people ties, which in turn support trade.

ul: **Energy and trade shock:** the Gulf conflict hits India’s oil and gas imports and trade routes, which is why Asian partners are being engaged for stability.
**Balance:** India engages the Quad, ASEAN and also Russia and China at once, which is the meaning of strategic autonomy.

prel.d: Association of Southeast Asian Nations; 11 members; the Philippines chairs in 2026.
Supersonic cruise missile of an Indo-Russian joint venture; the Philippines was its first export customer.
Naval drills of India, the U.S., Japan and Australia, now to include patrol aircraft.
A formal level of bilateral ties, here between India and the Philippines.

qs.q: ‘India’s Act East Policy has deepened ties with ASEAN.’ Discuss the recent outcomes and the challenges.
Discuss how India can balance its partnerships with the Quad, ASEAN, Russia and China.

topics.t: Xi hails ties with Russia ahead of the Shenzhen trilateral with Trump and Putin
topics.news: Chinese President Xi Jinping on Wednesday hailed relations with Russia as ‘a source of stability’ in a ‘turbulent’ world, even as he welcomed U.S. President Donald Trump with a rare airport reception a day before a trilateral summit in Shenzhen. Mr Xi opened the two-day APEC gathering with an address to a CEO Summit. Beijing has described the meeting of the three leaders on Thursday as of ‘groundbreaking significance’, and U.S. officials said they would discuss the war in Ukraine, the situation in Iran, global energy supply chains and nuclear arms control.

rows: APEC
Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation, a forum of 21 economies set up in 1989 for trade and economic cooperation; India is not a member.
China–Russia
A ‘no limits’ partnership was declared in February 2022; trade, energy and military ties have grown since the Ukraine war.
Three-way meeting
The first sit-down of the three leaders; it comes as arms-control limits on the U.S. and Russia have lapsed and China’s arsenal is growing.
India’s interest
A shift among the three powers on Ukraine, Iran, energy and arms control would affect India’s oil supplies, defence partners and the Indo-Pacific balance.

ul: **Reception as signal:** greeting a visiting leader at the airport is a rare mark of protocol, signalling Beijing’s wish for a warmer tone with Washington.
**Middle powers:** countries such as India watch to see whether a three-way understanding leaves their interests out.

prel.d: Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation, 21 economies, founded in 1989; India is not a member.
The Chinese city that hosts APEC 2026 and the three-way U.S.–China–Russia meeting.
India’s practice of independent decisions and ties with rival powers.
Strait through which a large share of the world’s oil passes.

qs.q: Examine how a thaw among the U.S., China and Russia would affect India’s foreign policy options.
What is APEC? Discuss its relevance for India, which is not a member.

topics.t: The average cost of a thali has jumped 16% in ten months
topics.news: The Hindu’s data analysis says food inflation climbed to 8.9% last month, the highest in at least 22 months of the new series and the highest this year. Prices of many items have risen sharply since January: onion by over 100% since March, garlic by 22% and rice by 11%. The analysis ties this largely to the prolonged U.S.–Iran war, which began with U.S. and Israeli attacks on Iran on 28 February, and to disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz that hit supplies of crude oil and fertilisers. The average cost of a vegetarian home-cooked meal has risen 16% since March; two thalis a day now cost a household about ₹2,515 a month, against about ₹2,205 a year ago and ₹1,847 five years ago, or 9.6% of average monthly wages of ₹26,310 (a Centre for Monitoring Indian Economy survey for September 2026), against 9.3% a year ago and 11.4% five years ago. Wages rose about 11% in a year, so the squeeze is smaller than prices alone suggest, but daily-wage households may struggle. The data come from the Consumer Affairs Ministry, the National Horticulture Board and CMIE.

rows: CPI
The Consumer Price Index measures retail inflation; food has a large weight, so food prices drive headline inflation. A new CPI series was introduced in 2026.
Supply shocks
War and shipping disruption raise the cost of oil, fertiliser and transport, and so of food.
Real wages
Wages adjusted for prices; if prices rise faster than wages, purchasing power falls.
Policy tools
Buffer stocks and open-market sales, import duty changes, stock limits and, for the poor, the public distribution system.
RBI
The Reserve Bank targets CPI inflation of 4% within a band of 2 to 6% and uses the repo rate.

ul: **Method:** the analysis assumes two thalis a day per family and omits spices, ghee and non-vegetarian meals, so the true cost is higher.
**Who is hit:** daily-wage households spend a large share of income on food.

prel.d: Consumer Price Index, the measure of retail inflation.
Rate of rise of food prices over a year.
Wages adjusted for changes in prices.
Strait through which much of the world’s oil and fertiliser trade passes.

qs.q: Discuss the causes and consequences of food inflation in India and the policy options to deal with it.
Poverty and malnutrition create a vicious cycle, hurting human capital. Discuss with reference to rising food costs.

topics.t: How AI could reshape global growth and productivity
topics.news: In the first of a two-part series in The Hindu, economists Rohit Azad and Indranil Chowdhury of the DevMac network ask whether artificial intelligence will prove as epoch-making as the steam engine or the internal combustion engine. A key expected effect is a big rise in labour productivity, the ratio of output to workers employed, which can rise if output grows for a given number of workers, if jobs are lost, or if jobs grow but output grows faster. They set out two schools. In the neoclassical, supply-side view (Robert Solow), output growth is the sum of labour-force growth and productivity growth, so a 2% workforce growth and 4% productivity growth settle at 6% growth, and productivity itself depends on human capital, research and development and patents (endogenous growth). In the heterodox, demand-side view, output that is not demanded is not produced, so unless productivity growth lifts demand, rising productivity affects jobs: if demand grows 3% and productivity 4%, jobs fall by 1%, and labour growth becomes the adjusting variable; labour supply has historically adjusted through migration, from the Atlantic slave trade to Bihar and Uttar Pradesh workers moving to Punjab. Chart 1 shows real output per worker in the U.S. sectors that adopt AI (information, finance and insurance, and professional and business services) at 148.17 in the second quarter of 2026 against 100 in 2012, well above the 120.61 that the 2012–19 trend implies. The authors say it is too early to be conclusive and that how widely the effect spreads is the open question; the second part will look at global macroeconomic effects.

rows: Labour productivity
Output divided by the number of workers employed.
Solow growth model
Robert Solow (Nobel Prize in Economics, 1987) showed that output growth depends on growth of labour and capital and of productivity, which he treated as outside the model.
Endogenous growth
Later theories (Paul Romer, Robert Lucas) explain productivity growth by investment in human capital, research and development and patent systems.
Heterodox demand-side view
Output is limited by demand, so the effect of higher productivity on jobs depends on whether demand grows faster or slower than productivity.
Migration
Workers moving from low-wage to high-wage regions or countries adjust the supply of labour to the demand for it.

ul: **Jobs and productivity:** if output demanded rises faster than productivity, more jobs are created; if slower, jobs fall.
**India’s response:** the IndiaAI Mission, approved in 2024 with an outlay of about ₹10,372 crore, funds computing power, datasets and skills.
**Open question:** the data cover U.S. sectors only, so the spread to the whole economy is yet to be seen.

prel.d: Output per worker employed.
Neoclassical growth model by Robert Solow, Nobel laureate of 1987.
Growth theory that explains productivity through human capital, research and innovation.
2024 Union Government mission, with an outlay of about ₹10,372 crore, to build India’s AI capacity.

qs.q: Discuss the likely impact of artificial intelligence on productivity, employment and growth. How should India prepare?
Distinguish the supply-side and demand-side views of economic growth. How does each see the effect of rising productivity on jobs?

topics.t: The need to expand Jan Aushadhi
topics.news: T. C. Suseel Kumar and R. Sudhakar write that the Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana has put low-cost medicines within reach but has not caught on as widely as India’s size and incomes warrant. A monthly medicines bill of ₹2,900 fell to ₹663 at a Jan Aushadhi outlet, they say. The scheme, launched in 2008 and revamped in 2015, runs through the Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Bureau of India and now covers 2,110 medicines and 315 surgical items. The network grew to 20,547 Kendras by end-July 2026 from 17,990 at the end of December 2025, with a target of 25,000 by March 2027, and 10 to 12 lakh visitors a day; sales at maximum retail price were ₹2,252 crore in 2025-26 and citizens saved about ₹9,000 crore that year, about 80% below market prices. Against about 12 lakh chemists, the Kendras are only about 1.7%. A study of 200 outpatients in Port Blair found only a third had heard of the scheme; a 2020 report counted 106 batches recalled over four years; the reported rate of substandard medicines is 0.34% against 3.70% in the open market; stock-outs and doctors’ reluctance to prescribe generics (a National Medical Commission order on generic names was put on hold) hurt trust. Their six steps: a national survey, regular published testing (the Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission has agreed to test random batches), online stock tracking, convincing doctors, promoting the Kendras for everyone, and funding. Medicines are 60–70% of households’ out-of-pocket health spending, and government health expenditure was 1.43% of GDP in 2023-24 against the National Health Policy’s 2.5% target for 2025.

rows: Generic medicine
A medicine sold under its chemical name, with the same active ingredient, strength and form as the branded one, usually at a lower price.
Jan Aushadhi
The scheme sells quality generics through Kendras at prices well below market; Jan Aushadhi Diwas is observed on 7 March.
Quality
Manufacturers must hold WHO-GMP certification and each batch is tested before supply.
Out-of-pocket spending
Medicines make up most of what households pay directly for health; insurance such as Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY mainly covers hospital stays, not outpatient drugs.
Public spending
The National Health Policy, 2017 set a target of 2.5% of GDP for public health spending by 2025.

ul: **Awareness and trust:** low awareness, stock-outs and doubts about quality limit use.
**Doctors’ role:** prescriptions by generic name would help, but doctors want assurance of quality first.

prel.d: Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana, the scheme for low-cost generic medicines, run by the Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Bureau of India.
A medicine sold under its chemical name at a lower price than the brand.
World Health Organization good manufacturing practice certification.
Money paid directly by households for health care.

qs.q: Discuss the role of generic medicines and the Jan Aushadhi scheme in reducing out-of-pocket health expenditure.
Examine the challenges before India’s health system in making medicines affordable and trusted.

topics.t: ‘Last local recruit’ of the Lashkar-e-Taiba killed in Kulgam
topics.news: Lateef Bhat, a 22-year-old accused of the terror attack on CRPF personnel the previous week, was killed on Wednesday outside a mosque in Zangalpora in Kulgam district, south Kashmir, after an eight-day operation. Police described him as the last local recruit of the Lashkar-e-Taiba and its last known active local terrorist in the Valley. He had hidden inside the mosque and turned down an offer to surrender, saying he was happy to meet Allah; he was shot dead about 50 metres from the mosque as he tried to escape the cordon. Senior Superintendent of Police Anayat Ali Choudhary said the forces had asked him to surrender with maximum restraint because he was inside a mosque, and a weapon was recovered. Another associate, Umar Nisar, was also killed in Kulgam the day before. Union Home Minister Amit Shah praised the synergy of the Jammu and Kashmir Police, the Army, the CRPF and intelligence agencies, and an Army spokesperson said the forces neutralised him by making him leave the mosque premises.

rows: Lashkar-e-Taiba
A Pakistan-based terror group formed around 1990 and responsible for the 2008 Mumbai attacks; it is listed as a terrorist organisation under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967.
Local recruitment
The number of local youth joining militant groups has fallen sharply in recent years, so most active militants are foreign.
Forces involved
The Jammu and Kashmir Police, the Army (Rashtriya Rifles), the Central Reserve Police Force and intelligence agencies run joint operations under a Unified Headquarters.
Protecting religious places
Security forces follow standing procedures to avoid damage to shrines and mosques, and to offer surrender before a final assault.

ul: **Proportionate force:** counter-terror operations aim to avoid harm to civilians and sacred places; offering surrender first is part of that approach.
**What next:** with local recruitment low, the Union Government’s focus is on cross-border infiltration, over-ground support networks and terror financing.

prel.d: Pakistan-based terror group behind the 2008 Mumbai attacks.
India’s main law against unlawful and terrorist activities and organisations.
Joint command of the Army, police and paramilitary in J&K counter-terror operations.
Village in Kulgam district where the operation took place.

qs.q: Discuss the changing nature of terrorism in Jammu and Kashmir and the measures taken to counter it.
Examine the challenges of conducting counter-terror operations in or near places of worship.

topics.t: Delhi’s November air best in ten years: the numbers and the measures
topics.news: Chief Minister Rekha Gupta said Delhi’s air quality this November has been the best for the month in the last 10 years, but that strict measures will continue as the challenging period lies ahead. Environment Minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa said the city has not had a single ‘severe’ day this season and recorded a record 220 clean-air days this year, whereas Novembers over the past 10 years often had four to six days above that level; the average AQI in the first half of November was about 170. The 24-hour average AQI on Wednesday was 232, up from 204 on Tuesday, and the Air Quality Early Warning System forecast ‘poor’ air on Thursday and ‘very poor’ on Friday because of unfavourable weather. The Government’s data: 25,610 vehicles challaned for pollution-certificate violations; 1,81,548 non-Delhi vehicles inspected, 30,742 turned back and 189 seized; 41,659 overage vehicles seized and 64,800 scrapped; 6,000 new EV charging points bringing the total to 14,913; 1,703 electric buses added out of 2,395 planned, with 692 more expected in December; road-sweeper shifts doubled to clean 4,000 km a day; action against about 12,000 polluting industrial units. Between 1 and 17 November, 8,874 construction and demolition sites were inspected, violations were found at 554, 112 were ordered closed, 462 got show-cause notices and compensation of over ₹2.65 crore was imposed. The Government aims to cut pollution by 10 to 15% every year.

blocks.h: Delhi’s air and the tools used

rows: AQI bands
Good 0–50, Satisfactory 51–100, Moderate 101–200, Poor 201–300, Very Poor 301–400, Severe 401–500.
PUC
A Pollution Under Control certificate shows that a vehicle’s emissions are within limits; vehicles without one can be challaned.
Overage vehicles
Delhi’s rules phase out older vehicles (generally 15 years for petrol and 10 for diesel) because of their higher emissions.
GRAP
The Graded Response Action Plan adds curbs as the AQI worsens; the Commission for Air Quality Management coordinates action across Delhi–NCR.
Seasonal factors
Winter cold, low winds and moisture trap pollutants; crop-residue burning in neighbouring States adds to the load.

ul: **Weather versus action:** a better month may reflect weather as well as measures, which is why year-round cuts in emissions matter.
**Single-day reading versus exposure:** daily AQI says little about long-term exposure, a point made in the day’s editorial.

prel.d: Air Quality Index, with six bands from Good to Severe.
Proof that a vehicle’s emissions are within limits.
System that forecasts air quality days ahead for Delhi.
Vehicles older than the legal limit, taken off Delhi’s roads.

qs.q: Mumbai, Delhi and Kolkata are mega cities with high air pollution. Discuss the causes and the measures taken to tackle it.
Evaluate the effectiveness of emergency measures such as GRAP compared with year-round emission reduction.

topics.t: Cyclone Akvan shifts course: uncertainty over landfall and intensity
topics.news: Severe cyclonic storm Akvan changed its path and, according to the IMD’s 8 p.m. bulletin on Wednesday, was set to make landfall between Narsapur in Andhra Pradesh and Puri in Odisha on 20 November. Its projected track kept changing: the first forecast showed it moving towards Machilipatnam or Bapatla in central Andhra Pradesh as a very severe cyclonic storm, a revised forecast said it may not intensify into one, and the track later shifted to Narsapur–Kakinada and then north towards north Andhra Pradesh and south Odisha. Experts blamed the uncertainty on El Niño, a poor distribution of ocean heat content and mid-level moisture, and said it might weaken further before landfall. The IMD issued a red alert for Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam, Alluri Sitarama Raju, Anakapalli and Kakinada districts and southern Odisha, and Andhra Pradesh’s Home Minister V. Anitha said 13 NDRF and 11 SDRF teams and fire service units were ready.

rows: Track errors
Cyclone tracks depend on steering winds and the surrounding systems; small shifts change the landfall point by hundreds of kilometres.
Ocean heat content
Warm water to a good depth feeds a cyclone; uneven heat limits its strengthening.
Mid-level moisture
Dry air in the middle atmosphere can weaken a storm by starving it of moisture.
El Niño
A warm phase in the Pacific that changes wind and heat patterns across the tropics, including the Indian Ocean.
Response forces
The National Disaster Response Force and the State Disaster Response Forces carry out rescue and relief.

ul: **Alerts and colour codes:** red means the authorities should take action; orange asks them to be prepared.
**Weaker does not mean safe:** even a weaker storm can bring heavy rain, flooding and a storm surge.

prel.d: Winds of 89 to 117 km/h on the IMD scale.
Heat stored in the upper ocean, a fuel for cyclones.
National and State Disaster Response Forces.
Warm phase of the Pacific that alters weather worldwide.

qs.q: What is the Fujiwhara effect? Explain its impact on the movement and intensity of tropical cyclones.
What factors make cyclone tracks and intensity hard to forecast? How do early warnings reduce loss of life?

topics.t: COVID-19 lessons for India’s response to air pollution
topics.news: In an editorial, Dr Soumya Swaminathan and Dr Chandrakant Lahariya argue that the COVID-19 response offers lessons for air pollution, which is still treated largely as a seasonal inconvenience. They note that an adult takes about 20,000–25,000 breaths a day, that the State of Global Air 2025 report estimated that more than two million deaths in India in 2023 were attributable to air pollution, and that a Lancet Planetary Health study put the economic loss at 1.36% of India’s GDP in 2019. Their seven lessons: strong political leadership and coordinated governance across Ministries and States; systematic data and a national environmental health surveillance platform linking air quality, weather, admissions and deaths; transparency, with public dashboards of annual PM2.5 exposure; outcome-based financing (a January 2026 CREA assessment found ₹13,415 crore released through the National Clean Air Programme and Finance Commission funding, about 74% used, with 68% spent on road dust, 14% on transport, 12% on waste and biomass burning, and under 1% each on industry and household fuel); separating emergency measures such as GRAP from sustained emission cuts; tightening standards, since India’s annual PM2.5 limit of 40 micrograms per cubic metre is eight times the WHO guideline of five; and public participation without shifting responsibility to individuals, since masks and purifiers do not cut pollution at its source.

rows: Health burden
Air pollution is linked to heart disease, stroke, chronic lung disease, lung cancer, diabetes and harm to pregnancy and children’s development, apart from respiratory illness.
NCAP
The National Clean Air Programme, launched in 2019, covers about 130 cities that do not meet the national standards.
Standards
India’s annual PM2.5 limit is 40 µg/m³; the WHO’s 2021 guideline is 5.
Source mix
PM2.5 comes from combustion, industry, transport, household fuels and chemical reactions of gases, so spending on road dust alone misses much of the problem.
Surveillance
Linking AQI with hospital and death data would show where the harm falls and whether measures work.

ul: **Equity:** poorer households, outdoor workers and children have the most exposure and the fewest resources.
**Outcome measure:** success should be judged by lower exposure and better health, not by the number of restrictions announced.

prel.d: Annual report on air pollution and health by the Health Effects Institute and partners.
National Clean Air Programme, launched in 2019.
Fine particles under 2.5 micrometres that reach deep into the lungs.
Funding linked to results such as lower exposure rather than to activity.

qs.q: Air pollution is a public health emergency. Discuss how the lessons of the COVID-19 response can improve India’s policy.
Examine the case for tighter national air-quality standards and a national environmental health surveillance system.

topics.t: Climate promises need to become praxis: finance, grids and a fair transition
topics.news: An opinion piece by Vipin Benny argues that climate promises must reach people as money, grids and jobs. At COP29 in Baku in 2024, countries agreed to provide up to $300 billion a year to developing countries by 2035 and called for mobilising $1.3 trillion a year from public and private sources; the test is whether funds arrive on time, at affordable prices and in a usable form, with grants, cheap loans and guarantees. India’s electricity demand is projected to grow about 6.4% a year over the next five years, according to the International Energy Agency. India reached 300.5 GW of non-fossil capacity by July 2026, over 60% of its 500 GW target for 2030, but installed capacity is not the same as electricity produced, and solar and wind are intermittent, so networks, storage and flexible power are needed. The renewable consumption obligation requires certain distribution companies and consumers to reach 43.33% renewable electricity by 2029-30. The article adds that a COP31 goal is to raise the share of electricity in final energy consumption to 35% by 2035, that coal workers need retraining, that electric buses are only as clean as the power that charges them, and that benefits should reach small firms and households.

rows: NCQG
The New Collective Quantified Goal on climate finance: at least $300 billion a year by 2035 as developed countries’ lead, within a wider call for $1.3 trillion.
India’s target for non-fossil electricity capacity; the 50% non-fossil share of installed capacity was reached earlier than planned.
RCO
The renewable consumption obligation, which sets minimum shares of renewable power for obligated entities under the Energy Conservation Act framework.
Carbon lock-in
Building long-lived fossil plants that keep emissions high for decades.
Just transition
Moving from coal while protecting workers and regions that depend on it.

ul: **Capacity versus generation:** a solar plant produces only in daylight, so its capacity factor is much lower than that of a coal plant.
**People-centric transition:** jobs in solar installation, battery maintenance and efficient manufacturing, and finance for small industry.

prel.d: New Collective Quantified Goal on climate finance set at COP29.
India’s goal of non-fossil electricity capacity by 2030.
Minimum renewable power share for obligated distribution companies and consumers.
Dependence on fossil infrastructure that is hard to leave.

qs.q: Examine the issues in climate finance for developing countries and India’s approach to the energy transition.
Why is installed renewable capacity not the same as electricity supplied? What does the grid need?

topics.t: A regulatory fix for educational campuses and environmental clearance
topics.news: Environmentalist Kalaiselvan Periyasamy writes that recent Supreme Court judgments have reaffirmed that educational buildings of over 20,000 square metres need prior Environmental Clearance under the EIA Notification, 2006, leaving institutions that built without it with no way to regularise them. The Notification had no built-up-area rule for educational institutions until a December 2014 exemption for schools, colleges and institutional hostels, which the Kerala High Court quashed in March 2024; a fresh exemption in January 2025 was stayed and then cancelled by the Supreme Court in August 2025. The Union’s 2017 Notification and 2021 Office Memorandum, which let violating projects seek clearance after the fact, were struck down in May 2025; after review, the Court’s final judgment on 29 July 2026 reaffirmed that prior clearance is mandatory and no fresh applications can be taken under them, but said the Government could bring a tailored, time-bound scheme through a valid statutory notification for categories of non-compliant projects with an overriding public interest. A Ministry Office Memorandum of 30 September 2026 says only pending applications may proceed. The author urges the Environment Ministry to issue a statutory notification for eligible campuses that covers environmental scrutiny, damage assessment, proportionate compensation and remediation, and that separates deliberate violations from developments made without intent.

rows: EIA Notification, 2006
Issued under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986; large projects such as buildings above a set built-up area need prior clearance after appraisal.
Ex post facto clearance
Clearance after construction has started; the Supreme Court in the Vanashakti case (May 2025) held it unlawful, and the final July 2026 judgment confirmed that prior clearance is mandatory.
Polluter pays
A violator bears the cost of damage and its repair, a principle the author wants built into any new scheme.
Statutory route
A fix must come through a valid statutory notification, not an office memorandum.

ul: **No blanket exemption:** the Court has not allowed exemption for educational buildings, and the author says a blanket exemption would also ignore environmental impact.
**Cost of delay:** the author warns that the gap could hinder the expansion of classrooms, laboratories and hostels and so the education goals of Viksit Bharat.

prel.d: Rule requiring prior Environmental Clearance for listed projects.
Approval given after a project has started or been built.
2025 Supreme Court ruling against clearance after the fact.
The polluter pays for the damage and for restoring the environment.

qs.q: Discuss the role of Environmental Impact Assessment in sustainable development. What are its limits?
Examine the issues in granting environmental clearance after construction (ex post facto clearance).
